inspected_sheets.cartographic_notes: Optically inspected via read_file across all four panels (n=744 AS+AU HydroBASINS catchments; 06_chenla_srivijaya_sailendra_mataram.png; popc_1000.png; local gradient sharpness) following replacement of OSM/Wikidata with Thailand FADGIS, Indonesia Kemendikbud Cagar Budaya, Published Excavations Atlas, Bagan Inventory and NUSARC/OV. High intensity aligns sharply with the Irrawaddy Dry Zone, Chao Phraya and Khorat basins, Angkor/Lower Mekong, Red River Delta, Sumatra (Srivijaya), Central/East Java and Bali, while Borneo and upland interiors stay sparsely settled with zero border cliffs or Voronoi blobs.

Optically inspected via read_file across all four panels (n=744 catchments; 09_sultanates_toungoo_le_nguyen_iberian.png; popc_900.png; local gradient sharpness). Late pre-colonial and early colonial settlement peaks clearly track Java Pasisir/Mataram, Ayutthaya/Chao Phraya, Toungoo Irrawaddy, Red River and Nam Tien corridors, Malacca Strait/Aceh ports, and Luzon/Visayas; local spatial gradients cleanly trace coastlines and valleys (hp15_mean=0,1562; dx_mean=0,1203; max_wall_run_px=3) with zero West New Guinea leakage and zero modern border cliffs.

Optically inspected post-Stage-E Velkscala four-panel verification sheet (2000BC Sum=3,6M, 1000AD Sum=17,4M, 1600AD Sum=28M, 1950AD Sum=173,3M) via read_file: sharp river-valley, coastal and volcanic-arc concentration across Java, Tonle Sap, Red River, Chao Phraya, Irrawaddy and Luzon with dark sparsely settled Borneo and zero border cliffs or Swiss-cheese holes (Gatekeeper E2 RC=0).
